response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS n FROM Orders o LEFT JOIN Invoices i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id), s AS (SELECT order_id, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT order_id, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_invoices, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: The 'average share' used as the threshold is computed over all orders, including zero-invoice ones. The returned 'average share' is the mean share of only the above-threshold orders. The excess is each such order's share minus the all-order average.
If there are no invoices at all, the total is 0 and every share is NULL, so the query returns a row of NULLs rather than raising an error.
